questions.question: Forcing a system into oscillation may cause resonance. For resonance the system must be driven at its: A natural frequency, B normal frequency, C optimum frequency, D damping frequency.
questions.answer: A - the natural frequency
steps: Resonance is a large-amplitude response that occurs when a system is driven at its natural frequency.
At the natural frequency the driving pushes are in phase with the motion, so energy transfer is most efficient.
Options B, C and D are not terms for the driving condition needed for resonance.
So the answer is A.

questions.question: Using the graph of energy absorbed by a water molecule against microwave frequency, comment on the website claim that water molecules absorb energy because they resonate.
questions.answer: The suggestion is not supported: the absorption peak is broad and lies at about 10 GHz, not at the oven frequency of 2.45 GHz, so the molecules are not being driven at a sharp resonance.
steps: Resonance would give a maximum energy absorption when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency, so the peak should be at the oven frequency of 2.45 GHz.
On the graph the peak is at about 10 GHz, roughly four times higher than 2.45 GHz, so the oven frequency does not coincide with the maximum.
At 2.45 GHz the absorption is well below the maximum value, and the peak is very broad (heavily damped) rather than the sharp peak expected for resonance.
So the molecules do absorb microwave energy at 2.45 GHz, but the graph does not show that this is because of resonance.

questions.question: Explain how the rotation of water molecules caused by microwave radiation cooks food.
questions.answer: Rotational kinetic energy is passed to neighbouring molecules by collisions, raising their internal energy and the food temperature.
steps: The oscillating microwave field makes polar water molecules rotate back and forth as they try to align with it.
Rotating molecules collide with and drag on neighbouring molecules, transferring kinetic energy to them.
The random kinetic energy of the molecules increases, which is an increase in the internal energy of the food.
The temperature of the food rises, so the energy is spread through the food and it is cooked.

questions.question: Suggest why microwave energy is transferred less efficiently to ice than to liquid water.
questions.answer: In ice the molecules are held in a fixed lattice and cannot rotate freely, so they absorb less microwave energy.
steps: Microwave heating works by making polar molecules rotate.
In ice the molecules are locked in a rigid lattice, so their rotation is restricted.
Less rotation means fewer collisions and less energy transferred into thermal energy.
So the energy transfer from the microwaves is less efficient for ice.

questions.question: 325 g of water is heated from 25.0 deg C to 85.0 deg C in 225 s by a 650 W oven. Assess the manufacturer's claim of 90% efficiency (c = 4190 J kg-1 K-1).
questions.answer: Efficiency is about 56%, so the 90% claim is not valid.
steps: Energy input = P t = 650 x 225 = 1.46 x 10^5 J.
Useful energy to heat the water = m c dT = 0.325 x 4190 x (85.0 - 25.0) = 8.17 x 10^4 J.
Efficiency = useful energy / energy input = 8.17 x 10^4 / 1.46 x 10^5 = 0.56.
An efficiency of 56% is well below 90%, so the claim is not valid.

questions.question: 325 g of hot water at 85.0 deg C is poured into a polystyrene beaker containing 62.5 g of ice at 0.0 deg C. Calculate the final temperature of the mixture (L = 3.33 x 10^5 J kg-1, c = 4190 J kg-1 K-1).
questions.answer: Final temperature = 58.5 deg C.
steps: Energy needed to melt the ice: Q = m L = 0.0625 x 3.33 x 10^5 = 2.08 x 10^4 J.
Energy lost by the hot water cooling to T: 0.325 x 4190 x (85.0 - T).
Energy gained by the melted ice warming from 0 to T: 0.0625 x 4190 x T.

questions.question: A simple pendulum takes 1.00 s to swing from one extreme position to the other. Which expression gives its length? (The option list is shown in the figure below.)
steps: Swinging from one extreme position to the other is half an oscillation, so the period is T = 2 x 1.00 s = 2.00 s.
For a simple pendulum T = 2 pi sqrt(L / g), so L = g T^2 / (4 pi^2).
Substituting T = 2.00 s gives L = (2.00)^2 x 9.81 / (4 pi^2) = 0.99 m, which is option B.
A uses T = 1.00 s (only half the period), and C and D have the expression upside down.

questions.question: State the conditions for a mass to undergo simple harmonic motion.
questions.answer: Acceleration is proportional to displacement from the equilibrium position and is always directed towards equilibrium.
steps: Simple harmonic motion needs a restoring force or acceleration.
The acceleration must be directly proportional to the displacement from the equilibrium position.
The acceleration must always be directed towards the equilibrium position, so a = -omega^2 x.
These two conditions together give sinusoidal motion.

questions.question: A 250 g mass hung from a spring extends it by 16.5 cm. The mass is then displaced a further 3.5 cm downwards and released. Calculate the maximum kinetic energy of the oscillating mass.
questions.answer: Maximum kinetic energy = 9.1 x 10^-3 J.
steps: Spring constant from the equilibrium extension: k = m g / x = 0.250 x 9.81 / 0.165 = 14.9 N m-1.
The amplitude is the extra 3.5 cm displacement, so A = 0.035 m.
Total energy of the oscillation is E = 1/2 k A^2 = 0.5 x 14.9 x 0.035^2 = 9.1 x 10^-3 J.
Energy is conserved, so the maximum kinetic energy (at equilibrium) equals this total energy: 9.1 x 10^-3 J.

questions.question: Add to the displacement-time graph of the oscillating mass a line showing how its kinetic energy varies over the same two cycles.
questions.answer: Draw a curve that is always positive, with a peak each time the displacement is zero and zero each time the displacement is at its maximum or minimum, so it repeats at twice the frequency of the displacement.
steps: Kinetic energy is zero at the extremes of the motion, where the mass is momentarily at rest. Mark KE = 0 at T/4, 3T/4, 5T/4 and 7T/4, where the displacement is at a maximum or minimum.
Kinetic energy is a maximum when the mass passes through equilibrium, where the displacement is zero: at t = 0, T/2, T, 3T/2 and 2T.
KE = KE_max cos^2(omega t), so the curve is a squared-cosine shape that never goes below the time axis and all its peaks are the same height.

Over the two displacement cycles the KE goes through four complete cycles (two per displacement cycle, 3 full humps plus a half hump at each end), so the KE frequency is double the displacement frequency.

questions.question: The mass is submerged in water and set into oscillation. Explain how the water affects the amplitude of oscillation.
questions.answer: Water exerts a drag (damping) force that removes energy, so the amplitude decreases more quickly over time.
steps: The water exerts a viscous drag force on the moving mass, opposing its motion.
This drag does negative work, transferring the oscillation energy into thermal energy in the water.
With less total energy, the amplitude of each swing becomes smaller.
So the oscillations are damped and die away more quickly than in air.

questions.question: A mass on a spring has period T. The same mass is hung on a spring with four times the spring constant. What is the new period? A T/4, B T/2, C 2T, D 4T.
questions.answer: B - T/2
steps: For a mass-spring system T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k).
The period is proportional to 1/sqrt(k), so with k four times larger T becomes T / sqrt(4).
The new period is T/2.
So the answer is B.

questions.question: State what is meant by simple harmonic motion.
questions.answer: Motion in which the acceleration is proportional to the displacement from equilibrium and is always directed towards equilibrium.
steps: SHM is oscillation in which the acceleration a is directly proportional to the displacement x from a fixed equilibrium point.
The acceleration is always directed towards the equilibrium position, so a = -omega^2 x.
This gives displacement, velocity and acceleration that vary sinusoidally with time.

questions.question: A bee's wings oscillate at 240 Hz and the wing tips have a maximum speed of 2.25 m s-1. Show that the amplitude is about 1.5 mm.
steps: For SHM the maximum speed is v_max = omega A = 2 pi f A.
Rearrange to give A = v_max / (2 pi f).
This is about 1.5 mm, as required.

questions.question: Calculate the maximum acceleration of the wing tip, given frequency 240 Hz and maximum speed 2.25 m s-1.
steps: Maximum acceleration a_max = omega^2 A = omega v_max.
omega = 2 pi f = 2 pi x 240 = 1508 rad s-1.

questions.question: State what is meant by an elastic material.
questions.answer: A material that returns to its original shape and size when the deforming force is removed.
steps: An elastic material deforms when a force is applied to it.
When the force is removed it recovers its original shape and length.
Within its limit it obeys Hooke's law, so extension is proportional to force.

questions.question: Explain what is meant by resonance.
questions.answer: Resonance is when a system is driven at its natural frequency, giving maximum amplitude and maximum energy transfer.
steps: Every system has a natural frequency at which it oscillates freely.
When an external periodic force drives it at this same frequency, each push is in phase with the motion.
Energy is transferred to the system most efficiently at this frequency.
So the amplitude of oscillation becomes a maximum.

questions.question: The wings oscillate at 240 Hz but the muscles only oscillate at 60 Hz. Suggest how impulses at 60 Hz can maintain the 240 Hz oscillation.
questions.answer: Each 60 Hz impulse acts once every four wing cycles, in the direction of motion, adding energy to offset damping.
steps: The wing's natural frequency is 240 Hz, which is 4 x 60 Hz.
Each muscle impulse therefore occurs once every four cycles of the wing motion.
If each impulse is timed to push in the direction of motion, it adds energy to the wing.
This replaces the energy lost to damping, so the 240 Hz oscillation is maintained.

questions.question: Give the SI base units of energy.
questions.answer: kg m^2 s^-2
steps: Energy is work done, E = F d.
Force F = m a, so E = m a d.
Using base units: kg x (m s-2) x m = kg m^2 s^-2, which is the joule.
The joule is a derived unit, but it is expressed here in the base units kg, m and s.

questions.question: Calculate the length of a simple pendulum that swings from one extreme position to the other in exactly 1.00 s.
questions.answer: Length = 0.99 m.
steps: One swing from one extreme to the other is half a period, so the full period T = 2.00 s.
For a simple pendulum T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g), so L = g T^2 / (4 pi^2).

questions.question: Suggest a disadvantage of basing the metre on the length of a seconds pendulum.
questions.answer: The length depends on local g, which varies with location and altitude, so the metre would not be the same everywhere.
steps: The period T = 2 pi sqrt(L/g) depends on the gravitational field strength g.
g varies slightly with latitude, altitude and local geology.
So a seconds pendulum would have different lengths at different places.
A standard of length should be the same everywhere, so this is a disadvantage.

questions.question: Over time the energy of oscillation of a car increases by a factor of 4. The amplitude of oscillation increases by what factor?
questions.answer: A factor of 2.
steps: The energy of SHM is E = 1/2 k A^2, so E is proportional to A^2.
If E increases by a factor of 4, then A^2 increases by a factor of 4.
So A increases by sqrt(4) = 2.
The amplitude doubles.

questions.question: The graph shows acceleration against time for an object in SHM. Which of graphs A to D shows displacement against time on the same x-axis scale?
questions.answer: A
steps: In SHM a = -omega^2 x, so the displacement graph is the acceleration graph turned upside down (same period, opposite sign).
The acceleration graph starts at zero and goes negative first, so the displacement starts at zero and goes positive first.
Only graph A starts at 0 and rises first. B starts below zero, C starts at a positive maximum, and D repeats the acceleration graph (going negative first).

questions.question: The graph shows acceleration against time for an object in SHM. Which of graphs A to D shows velocity against time?
questions.answer: C
steps: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph, so a = 0 at t = 0 means v is at a maximum or minimum there.
Just after t = 0 the acceleration is negative, so v is falling: the velocity starts at its positive maximum and decreases (v = v_max cos omega t).
The acceleration is most negative a quarter of a period later, when the velocity graph crosses zero going down, which also fits.
Only graph C starts at a maximum and falls. A and D start at zero and B starts at a negative value.

questions.question: An object oscillates with simple harmonic motion, period 0.55 s and amplitude 0.25 m. Which option shows a correct calculation of its maximum velocity? (Option letters are shown in the figure below.)
steps: The maximum velocity in SHM is v_max = omega A, with omega = 2 pi / T.
So v_max = (2 pi / 0.55) x 0.25 = 11.4 x 0.25 = 2.9 m s^-1, which is option B.
A multiplies by T instead of dividing, and C and D square the quantity, which would give an acceleration-type expression (omega^2 A), not a velocity.

questions.question: The velocity-time graph of a pendulum bob is given. Add a line showing how its displacement varies with time over the same interval.
questions.answer: Draw a sine curve of displacement with the same period of 2.0 s: zero at t = 0, a maximum at 0.5 s, zero at 1.0 s, a minimum at 1.5 s, zero at 2.0 s, and so on up to 4.0 s.
steps: Velocity is the gradient of the displacement-time graph. The velocity is a maximum at t = 0, so the displacement curve is steepest there and passes through zero going upwards.
The velocity is zero at 0.5 s, 1.5 s, 2.5 s and 3.5 s, so the displacement is at a maximum or minimum at those times: maxima at 0.5 s and 2.5 s, minima at 1.5 s and 3.5 s.

The displacement is a sine curve with the same period (2.0 s) as the velocity; it lags the velocity by a quarter of a cycle (0.5 s). The graph has no displacement scale, so any sensible amplitude is accepted.

questions.question: Using the velocity-time graph of the pendulum bob, determine the length of the simple pendulum.
questions.answer: L = 0.99 m (about 1.0 m)
steps: The velocity is a maximum at t = 0 and again at t = 2.0 s, so the period is T = 2.0 s (the velocity is also zero at 0.5 s, 1.5 s and 2.5 s, which agrees).
For a simple pendulum T = 2 pi sqrt(L / g), so L = g T^2 / (4 pi^2).

questions.question: Describe when the use of a data logger is an advantage over other measuring instruments.
questions.answer: When a quantity changes quickly or must be recorded over a long time, since a data logger takes many readings automatically.
steps: A data logger takes many readings automatically at a high and fixed rate.
It is useful when the quantity changes quickly, such as a short-period oscillation, which a person with a stopwatch cannot follow.
It is also useful for recording over long periods without a person present.
It gives a precise time-stamped record that can be analysed on a computer.

questions.question: A train crosses a bridge which is forced into resonant oscillation. Which happens only when resonance occurs? A Damping reduces the amplitude. B Energy is transferred from the train to the bridge. C Resistive forces dissipate energy from the train. D The amplitude of oscillation is unusually large.
questions.answer: D - the amplitude of oscillation is unusually large.
steps: Damping, energy transfer from the train and resistive dissipation happen in all forced oscillations, not only at resonance.
Resonance is specifically the condition where the driving frequency matches the natural frequency and the amplitude becomes very large.
Option D describes that effect and is true only at resonance.
So the answer is D.

questions.question: Explain why a mass on a spring that obeys Hooke's law moves with simple harmonic motion when set oscillating.
questions.answer: The restoring force is proportional to the displacement and acts towards equilibrium, so the acceleration is proportional to and opposite to the displacement.
steps: By Hooke's law the spring force is F = -k x, proportional to the displacement and directed back towards equilibrium.
At equilibrium the weight balances the spring force; about this point the net restoring force is -k x.
Newton's second law gives a = F/m = -(k/m) x.
So the acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed towards equilibrium, which is SHM.

questions.question: With a mass of 0.200 kg in equilibrium the spring extension is 7.50 cm. Show that the stiffness k is about 26 N m-1.
steps: At equilibrium the weight equals the spring force: m g = k x.
This matches the value required.

questions.question: Using the graph of frequency against mass for the spring, determine a value for the stiffness k and deduce whether it is consistent with the value in part (i).
questions.answer: k = 27 N m^-1, which is consistent with 26 N m^-1 (a difference of only about 3 to 4%)
steps: f = (1 / 2 pi) sqrt(k / m), so f^2 = (k / 4 pi^2) x (1 / m). The gradient of the f^2 against 1/m graph is therefore k / 4 pi^2.
Take a large triangle on the best-fit line: it passes through (0.22, 0.0) and (5.0, 3.27), so the gradient = 3.27 / (5.0 - 0.22) = 0.68 Hz^2 kg.
k = 4 pi^2 x gradient = 4 pi^2 x 0.68 = 27 N m^-1.
The two values differ by only about 3%, which is smaller than the uncertainty from drawing a line through the scattered points, so the graph gives a value of k consistent with part (i).

questions.question: The graph shows acceleration against displacement for a mass in SHM. Which expression gives its period? (Graph and options A to D are shown in the figure below.)
steps: In SHM a = -omega^2 x, so the gradient of the a-x graph has magnitude omega^2 = 3.2 / 0.20 = 16 s^-2, giving omega = 4.0 rad s^-1.
T = 2 pi / omega = 2 pi / sqrt(3.2 / 0.20) = 2 pi x sqrt(0.20 / 3.2) = 1.6 s, which is option D.
C has the ratio the wrong way up (it would give 2 pi omega), and A and B are missing the square root.

questions.question: A mass oscillates with SHM at frequency 0.5 Hz and amplitude 0.3 m. Which expression gives its maximum velocity in m s-1? (Option list is shown in the figure below.)
steps: The maximum velocity is v_max = omega A, and omega = 2 pi f, so v_max = 2 pi f A.
v_max = 2 pi x 0.5 x 0.3 = 0.94 m s^-1, which is option C.
A and B use 2 pi / f, which is not the angular frequency, and B and D use 0.15 m, which is not the amplitude.

questions.question: The gravitational field strength on the Moon is one sixth of that on Earth. A pendulum has period T on Earth. What is its period on the Moon?
questions.answer: D: T sqrt(6) = 2.4 T
steps: For a simple pendulum T = 2 pi sqrt(L / g), so T is proportional to 1 / sqrt(g).
On the Moon g is one sixth as large, so the period is multiplied by sqrt(6) = 2.4: T_Moon = T sqrt(6), which is option D.
A weaker gravitational field gives a smaller restoring force, so the pendulum swings more slowly and the period gets longer.

questions.question: Explain how an alternating current in the coil of a loudspeaker makes the cone oscillate at the frequency of the current.
questions.answer: The current in the coil in the magnetic field gives a force F = BIL that reverses with the alternating current, so the cone oscillates at the same frequency.
steps: The coil carries a current while it sits in the magnetic field of the permanent magnet.
A force F = BIL acts on the coil, perpendicular to both the field and the current.
The alternating current reverses each half cycle, so the force reverses at the frequency of the current.
The coil and cone are pushed in and out, so the cone oscillates at the frequency of the alternating current.

questions.question: The coil moves with SHM through a maximum distance of 3.5 mm while the loudspeaker emits a 75 Hz sound. Calculate the maximum velocity of the coil.
questions.answer: v_max = 1.6 m s-1 (about 1.65 m s-1).
steps: Maximum velocity v_max = omega A = 2 pi f A.
The amplitude is the maximum distance from equilibrium, A = 3.5 x 10^-3 m.
So the maximum velocity is about 1.6 m s-1.

questions.question: State the position of the coil when its velocity is a maximum.
questions.answer: At the equilibrium (central) position, where the displacement is zero.
steps: In SHM the speed is greatest when the displacement is zero.
This is the equilibrium position, where the restoring force and acceleration are zero.
At the extremes of the motion the velocity is zero instead.

questions.question: At a particular frequency the loudspeaker cone starts to oscillate with a very large amplitude. Explain why.
questions.answer: The driving frequency matches the natural frequency of the cone, so resonance occurs.
steps: The coil drives the cone at the frequency of the alternating current.
At one particular frequency the driving frequency equals the natural frequency of the cone.
Energy is then transferred to the cone most efficiently, so the amplitude becomes very large.

questions.question: State the conditions for simple harmonic motion, applied to the man and diving board oscillating.
questions.answer: Acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and is always directed towards equilibrium.
steps: SHM needs a restoring force or acceleration proportional to displacement from equilibrium.
The restoring force or acceleration must always act towards the equilibrium position.
For the board, the restoring force comes from the elastic bending of the board (Hooke's law).
Together these conditions give approximate SHM.

questions.question: A man of mass 75 kg stands on the board, giving an equilibrium displacement of 18 cm. Show that the stiffness of the board is about 4000 N m-1.
steps: At equilibrium the spring force balances the weight: k x = m g.
k = 4.09 x 10^3 N m-1, which is about 4000 N m-1.
This confirms the value required.

questions.question: Calculate the frequency of oscillation of the man on the board, ignoring the mass of the board (k about 4000 N m-1, m = 75 kg).
steps: For a mass-spring system f = (1/2 pi) sqrt(k/m).
Use k = 4.09 x 10^3 N m-1 from part (i) and m = 75 kg.
So the frequency is about 1.2 Hz.

questions.question: If the amplitude is large enough, the man loses contact with the board at a point above equilibrium. Explain why.
questions.answer: Above equilibrium the downward acceleration can exceed g; the board cannot pull the man down, so the contact force becomes zero and he leaves the board.
steps: Above equilibrium the man's acceleration is directed downwards, towards equilibrium, with magnitude omega^2 x.
The contact force R acts upwards, so m g - R = m a and R = m (g - a).
If a is greater than g, R would have to be negative, and a board can only push upwards.
So at large amplitude the contact force falls to zero above equilibrium and the man loses contact.

questions.question: A glass is gently struck and emits sound for a short time. When a wet finger is slid around its rim it produces a loud continuous sound. Explain these observations using resonance.
questions.answer: Striking gives free oscillation at the natural frequency that decays through damping; the wet finger forces the glass at its natural frequency, so resonance gives a loud steady sound.
steps: Striking the glass gives a sudden impulse, so it oscillates freely at its natural frequency.
Damping (energy loss to the air and the glass) removes energy, so the sound dies away quickly.
Sliding a wet finger causes repeated stick-slip impulses on the rim, which act as a periodic driving force.
If the driving frequency matches the natural frequency of the glass, resonance occurs and energy is transferred efficiently.
The amplitude becomes large, giving a loud continuous sound while the finger is moved.

questions.question: The graph shows the water level in the Bay of Fundy over a 7-day period. Determine the period T of the water level, in hours.
questions.answer: T = 12.4 hours (about 12 to 13 hours)
steps: Measure over many cycles to reduce the reading error: the first peak is at about 0.33 days and the 13th peak at about 6.54 days, which is 12 complete cycles.
Time for 12 cycles = 6.54 - 0.33 = 6.21 days, so T = 6.21 / 12 = 0.52 days.
T = 0.52 x 24 = 12.4 hours (consistent with the usual interval between successive high tides of about 12.4 h).

questions.question: The natural period of water in the bay is between 12 and 13 hours. Explain why unusually high tides are observed.
questions.answer: The natural period is close to the tidal forcing period, so resonance occurs and the water level builds up to a large amplitude.
steps: The Moon's gravity drives the water level with a period of about 12 hours.
The natural period of water in the bay is 12 to 13 hours, close to this driving period.
When the driving frequency is close to the natural frequency, resonance occurs.
Energy is transferred efficiently, so the water oscillates with large amplitude, giving unusually high tides.

questions.question: The graph shows velocity against time for a mass in SHM. Which of graphs A to D shows displacement from equilibrium against time over the same interval?
questions.answer: A
steps: Velocity is the gradient of the displacement-time graph. At t = 0 the velocity is zero, so the displacement is at a maximum or minimum there.
Just after t = 0 the velocity is negative, so the displacement is decreasing: it starts at its positive maximum and falls (y = A cos omega t).
The velocity is zero again after half a period, where the displacement has its minimum, which matches A.
B starts at a minimum, and C and D start at zero, so none of them fits.

questions.question: The frequency of oscillation of a mass on a spring doubles, with the amplitude unchanged. Which quantity is also doubled? A maximum acceleration, B maximum kinetic energy, C maximum velocity, D period.
questions.answer: C - the maximum velocity.
steps: For fixed amplitude A, omega = 2 pi f doubles when f doubles.
Maximum velocity v_max = omega A doubles, so option C is doubled.
Maximum acceleration omega^2 A quadruples (A is wrong), the maximum kinetic energy does not double (B is wrong), and the period halves (D is wrong).
So the answer is C.

questions.question: In the Pantheon in Paris a pendulum takes 8.25 s to swing from one extreme position to the other. Which expression gives its length? (Option list is shown in the figure below.)
steps: Swinging from one extreme position to the other is half an oscillation, so T = 2 x 8.25 s = 16.5 s.
T = 2 pi sqrt(L / g), so L = g T^2 / (4 pi^2).
L = (16.5)^2 x 9.81 / (4 pi^2) = 67.7 m, which is option D.
C uses 8.25 s (half the period), and A and B have the expression upside down.

questions.question: A mass oscillates with SHM about a fixed point O. Which statement is correct? A Its velocity is always towards O. B Its acceleration is always towards O. C Its acceleration is proportional to its velocity. D Its acceleration and velocity are always in opposite directions.
questions.answer: B - its acceleration is always towards O.
steps: In SHM the acceleration is always directed towards the equilibrium point O.
The velocity is not always towards O, since it reverses direction on each side of O, so A is false.
Acceleration is proportional to displacement, not to velocity (C is false).
Acceleration and velocity are not always opposite (D is false), so the answer is B.

questions.question: The suspension system of a car is forced into vertical oscillation. Which row of the table shows how the maximum amplitude A0 and its frequency f0 change as damping is reduced?
questions.answer: D: A0 increases and f0 increases
steps: Less damping means less energy is dissipated per cycle, so the amplitude at resonance gets larger: A0 increases.
With heavy damping the amplitude peak occurs at a frequency below the natural frequency. As the damping is reduced the peak sharpens and moves towards the natural frequency, so f0 increases.
So both quantities increase, which is row D.

questions.question: State the conditions necessary for an object to move with simple harmonic motion.
questions.answer: Acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and is always directed towards equilibrium.
steps: The acceleration must be directly proportional to the displacement from equilibrium.
The acceleration must always be directed towards the equilibrium position.
Together these give a = -omega^2 x, which describes SHM.
Both conditions must be stated for full marks.

questions.question: The bracket has a highest to lowest distance of 8.0 cm and completes 270 oscillations per minute. Sketch a velocity-time graph for the bracket, including velocity and time values.
questions.answer: A sinusoidal v-t graph with peaks at +1.1 m s^-1 and -1.1 m s^-1 (1.13 m s^-1) and a period of 0.22 s.
steps: Frequency f = 270 / 60 = 4.5 Hz, so the period T = 1 / 4.5 = 0.22 s and omega = 2 pi f = 28.3 rad s^-1.
The distance from highest to lowest position is 8.0 cm, so the amplitude is A = 4.0 cm = 0.040 m.
The maximum velocity is v_max = omega A = 28.3 x 0.040 = 1.13 m s^-1.
Draw a smooth sine (or cosine) curve centred on v = 0 and label the peaks +1.13 and -1.13 m s^-1 on the velocity axis.
Scale the time axis so that one complete cycle takes 0.22 s (a quarter cycle is 0.056 s, so the zero crossings and peaks fall at multiples of 0.056 s: 0.056, 0.11, 0.17, 0.22 s).
Either starting phase is acceptable (starting at zero, or starting at a peak) provided the amplitude and the period are labelled.

questions.question: Determine the maximum acceleration of the bracket, given amplitude 4.0 cm and 270 oscillations per minute.
questions.answer: a_max = 32 m s-2.
steps: Frequency f = 270 / 60 = 4.5 Hz, and omega = 2 pi f = 28.3 rad s-1.
The amplitude is half the distance between extremes, A = 4.0 x 10^-2 m.

questions.question: Suggest why the paint particles in the can experience a maximum acceleration different from the answer to part (ii).
questions.answer: The paint is not rigidly fixed to the bracket, so it can oscillate with a different amplitude or phase from the bracket.
steps: The bracket drives the can, but the paint particles are not rigidly attached to the bracket.
The can and paint can move as a forced system with damping and a different response.
The particles may therefore have a different amplitude and phase, giving a different maximum acceleration.
So the paint's acceleration is not simply omega^2 times the bracket amplitude.

questions.question: A mass displaced 5 cm from equilibrium oscillates; its acceleration against displacement graph is given. Sketch a graph of displacement against time.
questions.answer: A sinusoidal x-t graph of amplitude 5 cm and period about 5.0 s, e.g. a cosine curve starting at +5 cm.
steps: The gradient of the a-x graph is -8 / 5 = -1.6 s^-2, so omega^2 = 1.6 s^-2 and omega = 1.26 rad s^-1 (the acceleration axis is in cm s^-2).
T = 2 pi / omega = 2 pi / 1.26 = 5.0 s.
The mass is displaced 5 cm and released, so it starts at rest at maximum displacement and the amplitude is 5 cm: x = 5 cos(1.26 t) cm.

Sketch a cosine curve: +5 cm at t = 0, zero at about 1.25 s, -5 cm at about 2.5 s, zero at about 3.7 s and back to +5 cm at 5.0 s. Label x = +5 and -5 cm on the axis and the time values on the t axis.

questions.question: A seconds pendulum has a period of 2 s. Which expression gives its length in metres? (Option list is shown in the figure below.)
steps: T = 2 pi sqrt(L / g), so L = g T^2 / (4 pi^2).
This is option C. A and B are not in the right form, and D (9.81 / 4 pi^2) would be the length for T = 1 s.

questions.question: Add to the graph of elastic potential energy against displacement a line showing how the total energy of the mass-spring system varies with displacement.
questions.answer: A horizontal straight line at the total energy of about 19 mJ, from x = -2 cm to x = +2 cm, meeting the curve at both ends.
steps: In SHM the total energy (elastic potential plus kinetic) is constant, so it is a horizontal line.

At the maximum displacement (the amplitude, 2.0 cm) the mass is momentarily at rest, so all the energy is elastic potential energy. The line is therefore at the height where the curve ends, about 19 mJ.
At any other displacement, the gap between the horizontal line and the curve is the kinetic energy.

questions.question: Using the EPE-displacement graph for a 150 g mass on a vertical spring, determine the speed of the mass when its displacement is 1.0 cm.
steps: The total energy equals the potential energy at the amplitude (2.0 cm), which is about 19 mJ.
At a displacement of 1.0 cm the graph gives an elastic potential energy of about 4.5 mJ.
Kinetic energy at 1.0 cm = 19 - 4.5 = 14.5 mJ = 1.45 x 10^-2 J.

questions.question: Explain why the amplitude of vibration of the car body on its suspension increases at a particular speed.
questions.answer: The bump spacing gives a driving frequency equal to the natural frequency of the suspension, so resonance occurs.
steps: The speed bumps drive the car body with frequency f = v / spacing.
At one particular speed this driving frequency equals the natural frequency of the suspension.
At resonance energy is transferred to the car body most efficiently.
So the amplitude of vibration becomes very large.

questions.question: A 65 kg person getting into a car with empty mass 1300 kg lowers its height by 2.5 cm. Resonance occurs when speed bumps are 25 m apart. Treating the car as a mass-spring system, calculate the speed of the car.
questions.answer: v = 17.6 m s-1, about 18 m s-1.
steps: Stiffness from the compression: k = m g / x = 65 x 9.81 / 0.025 = 2.55 x 10^4 N m-1.
Natural period of the car: T = 2 pi sqrt(m / k) = 2 pi sqrt(1300 / 2.55 x 10^4) = 1.42 s.
At resonance the bump spacing is passed in one natural period of oscillation.
Speed v = spacing / T = 25 / 1.42 = 17.6 m s-1, about 18 m s-1.

questions.question: Explain how damping reduces the large amplitude of vibration of the car on its suspension.
questions.answer: Damping dissipates energy from the oscillation (for example as heat in the shock absorbers), so the amplitude falls.
steps: Damping forces oppose the motion of the suspension and do negative work on it.
This converts the kinetic and potential energy of the oscillation into thermal energy.
With less energy in the oscillation the amplitude decreases.
Damping also reduces the peak amplitude at resonance.

questions.question: A mass on a spring oscillates vertically with damping. Which statement is correct? A The damping force is always opposite to the acceleration. B The damping force is always opposite to the velocity. C The damping force is always in the same direction as the acceleration. D The damping force is always in the same direction as the velocity.
questions.answer: B - the damping force is always opposite to the velocity.
steps: Damping is a resistive force that opposes the motion of the oscillating mass.
Therefore it is always opposite in direction to the velocity.
It is not necessarily opposite to the acceleration, so A is wrong.
So the answer is B.

questions.question: Which describes a ductile material? A A material that behaves elastically under tension. B A material that has a large plastic deformation before it breaks. C A material with a large breaking stress. D A material with a large Young modulus.
questions.answer: B - a material with large plastic deformation before it breaks.
steps: A ductile material can be stretched a large amount permanently before it fractures.
This large plastic deformation absorbs energy and so damps oscillations.
Elastic behaviour (A), breaking stress (C) and Young modulus (D) do not define ductility.
So the answer is B.

questions.question: The graph shows velocity against time for a particle in SHM. Which graph shows displacement against time over the same interval?
questions.answer: B
steps: Velocity is the gradient of the displacement-time graph. At t = 0 the velocity is zero, so the displacement is at a maximum or minimum.
Just after t = 0 the velocity is positive, so the displacement is increasing, which means it starts at its negative maximum (x = -A cos omega t).
Only B starts at a minimum and rises. A starts at zero and rises, C starts at zero and falls, and D starts at a positive maximum.

questions.question: Using the student's timings for 30 oscillations of a mass on the springs labelled k = 21 N m-1, deduce whether the label is correct.
questions.answer: The label is correct: the calculated stiffness of each spring is 20.9 N m^-1, which is 21 N m^-1 to 2 significant figures.
steps: The two identical springs are side by side supporting the mass (in parallel), so the combined stiffness is 2k and T = 2 pi sqrt(m / 2k).
Combined stiffness = 4 pi^2 m / T^2 = 4 pi^2 x 0.22 / (0.456)^2 = 41.8 N m^-1.
Each spring: k = 41.8 / 2 = 20.9 N m^-1, which agrees with the label of 21 N m^-1.

questions.question: The hand is oscillated at increasing frequency with constant amplitude. The mass's amplitude rises to a maximum and then falls. Explain this observation.
questions.answer: The amplitude is greatest when the driving frequency equals the natural frequency (resonance); on either side the energy transfer is less efficient, so the amplitude falls.
steps: As the driving frequency rises towards the natural frequency of the mass, each push adds energy in phase and the amplitude grows.
At the natural frequency resonance occurs, so the amplitude reaches its maximum.
Beyond this the driving pushes become out of phase with the motion, so less energy is transferred and the amplitude falls.
Damping also removes energy, which limits the peak amplitude.

questions.question: A student concludes that because the amplitude increases to a maximum, energy conservation does not apply. Explain whether this conclusion is correct.
questions.answer: The conclusion is not correct: the hand does work on the system, so the extra energy is supplied from outside, and energy is still conserved.
steps: Energy conservation applies to all situations, including resonance.
The hand does work on the spring-mass system, supplying energy at the driving frequency.
The amplitude grows because energy input exceeds the energy lost to damping, so the mass gains energy.
The energy from the hand equals the increase in stored energy plus the energy dissipated, so energy is conserved.

questions.question: A 150 g mass stretches a spring by 7.5 cm and is displaced 3.0 cm from equilibrium and released. Explain why its motion is simple harmonic.
questions.answer: The restoring force is proportional to displacement (Hooke's law) and directed towards equilibrium, so the acceleration is proportional to and opposite to the displacement.
steps: The spring obeys Hooke's law, so the restoring force F = -k x is proportional to the displacement.
At equilibrium the spring force balances the weight, so the net force about equilibrium is -k x.
Newton's second law gives a = -(k/m) x, which is proportional to displacement and directed towards equilibrium.
This satisfies the conditions for SHM.

questions.question: Calculate the maximum velocity of the 150 g mass that stretched the spring by 7.5 cm and oscillates with amplitude 3.0 cm.
questions.answer: v_max = 0.34 m s-1.
steps: Spring constant k = m g / x = 0.150 x 9.81 / 0.0750 = 19.6 N m-1.
Angular frequency omega = sqrt(k/m) = sqrt(19.6 / 0.150) = 11.4 rad s-1.
Amplitude A = 3.0 cm = 0.030 m, the displacement from equilibrium.
Maximum velocity v_max = omega A = 11.4 x 0.030 = 0.34 m s-1.

questions.question: Explain why the maximum velocity of the oscillating mass decreased over time.
questions.answer: Air resistance (damping) does negative work on the mass, removing energy, so the amplitude and maximum velocity decrease.
steps: Air resistance and internal friction (damping) oppose the motion and do negative work on the mass.
This removes energy from the oscillation, so the total energy falls.
Lower energy means a smaller amplitude.
Since v_max = omega A, the maximum velocity decreases.

questions.question: A simple pendulum's frequency is determined, then its length is doubled. By what factor is the frequency multiplied? (Option list is shown in the figure below.)
steps: For a simple pendulum f = (1 / 2 pi) sqrt(g / L), so f is proportional to 1 / sqrt(L).
If L is doubled, f is multiplied by 1 / sqrt(2) = 0.71, which is option A.

questions.question: A baby's heart beats at 142 beats per minute and the heart wall has a maximum velocity of 22.0 mm s-1. Assuming simple harmonic motion, calculate the maximum displacement of the wall in mm.
questions.answer: Maximum displacement = 1.48 mm, about 1.5 mm.
steps: Frequency f = 142 / 60 = 2.37 Hz.
Maximum velocity v = omega A = 2 pi f A, so A = v / (2 pi f).
So the maximum displacement is about 1.5 mm.

questions.question: The motion of the baby's heart wall only approximates to simple harmonic motion. State what is meant by simple harmonic motion.
questions.answer: Motion in which the acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and always directed towards equilibrium.
steps: SHM is oscillation in which the acceleration is proportional to the displacement from a fixed equilibrium point.
The acceleration is always directed towards the equilibrium position.
This gives sinusoidal variation of displacement with time.

questions.question: An object oscillates with SHM, period 0.65 s and amplitude 0.12 m. Which expression gives its maximum velocity? (Option list is shown in the figure below.)
steps: The maximum velocity is v_max = omega A with omega = 2 pi / T.
v_max = (2 pi / 0.65) x 0.12 = 9.67 x 0.12 = 1.2 m s^-1, which is option B.
A multiplies by T instead of dividing, and C and D are squared, which would give a maximum acceleration-type expression.

questions.question: The graph shows acceleration against time for a particle in SHM. Which graph shows velocity against time over the same interval?
questions.answer: B
steps: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph, so a = 0 at t = 0 means v is at a maximum or minimum there.
Just after t = 0 the acceleration is positive, so v is increasing: the velocity starts at its negative maximum and rises (v = -v_max cos omega t).
A quarter of a period later the acceleration is at its maximum, which is where the velocity graph crosses zero going up. Only B starts at a minimum and rises.
A starts at zero and rises, C starts at zero and falls, and D starts at a positive maximum.

questions.question: A simple pendulum in SHM has acceleration a and displacement x. Which of graphs A to D shows how a varies with x?
questions.answer: D
steps: In SHM the acceleration is proportional to the displacement and always acts towards the equilibrium position: a = -omega^2 x.
So the graph of a against x is a straight line through the origin with a negative gradient, which is graph D.
B has a positive gradient (acceleration away from equilibrium), and A and C show a constant acceleration.

questions.question: During an earthquake steel-framed buildings remove energy from the oscillation of the building. Which is the reason? A Steel is a ductile material. B Steel is an elastic material. C Steel is a stiff material. D Steel is a strong material.
questions.answer: A - steel is ductile, so it deforms plastically and dissipates energy as heat.
steps: Energy is removed when the steel deforms permanently (plastically) during the oscillation.
Ductile materials undergo large plastic deformation, converting kinetic energy into thermal energy.
Elasticity, stiffness and strength do not remove energy from an oscillation.
So the answer is A.

questions.question: Explain why astronauts in orbit are described as weightless, even though they experience a weight force.
questions.answer: The astronauts and the station are both in free fall with the same acceleration, so there is no contact (normal) force on the astronauts.
steps: The station and the astronauts are continuously falling towards the Earth under gravity.
They have the same acceleration, so there is no contact force between them and the station.
The sensation of weightlessness comes from the absence of a normal (contact) force, although gravity still acts.
So the weight force exists but no reaction force is felt.

questions.question: A force of 175 N deforms the spring by 28.9 cm. The chair oscillates with period 0.858 s when empty and 2.26 s with an astronaut sitting in it. Calculate the mass of the astronaut.
questions.answer: Mass of astronaut = 67 kg.
steps: Stiffness k = F / x = 175 / 0.289 = 605.5 N m-1.
Chair plus astronaut: m = k T^2 / (4 pi^2) = 605.5 x 2.26^2 / 39.48 = 78.3 kg.
Mass of astronaut = 78.3 - 11.3 = 67 kg.

questions.question: A mass hung on a spring oscillates with frequency f. The mass is doubled. What is the new frequency? (Option list is shown in the figure below.)
questions.answer: B: f / sqrt(2) = 0.71 f
steps: For a mass on a spring f = (1 / 2 pi) sqrt(k / m), so f is proportional to 1 / sqrt(m).
If the mass is doubled, f is multiplied by 1 / sqrt(2), so the new frequency is f / sqrt(2) = 0.71 f, which is option B.

questions.question: A mass oscillates with SHM. Which statement about its acceleration is correct? A Always opposite to velocity. B Always same direction as velocity. C Always away from equilibrium. D Always towards equilibrium.
questions.answer: D - the acceleration is always towards the equilibrium position.
steps: In SHM the acceleration is proportional to displacement and directed opposite to it.
So the acceleration always points towards the equilibrium position.
It is not always opposite to velocity or always in the same direction as velocity, so A and B are wrong.
Option C is the opposite of the correct statement, so the answer is D.

questions.question: A mass in SHM has angular velocity 2 rad s-1 and maximum velocity 10 cm s-1. Which expression gives the amplitude in cm? (Option list is shown in the figure below.)
steps: The maximum velocity is v_max = omega A, so A = v_max / omega.
A = 10 cm s^-1 / 2 rad s^-1 = 5 cm, which is option B.
A has the ratio the wrong way up, and C and D contain sin 2t, which would be an expression for a value at a particular time and not the amplitude.

questions.question: A mass-spring system has maximum kinetic energy E. The amplitude is doubled. What is the new maximum kinetic energy? A 4E, B 2E, C E, D 0.5E.
questions.answer: A - 4E.
steps: Maximum kinetic energy equals the total energy 1/2 k A^2, which is proportional to A^2.
Doubling A multiplies A^2 by 4.
So the new maximum kinetic energy is 4E.
The answer is A.

questions.question: The graph shows velocity against time for an object in SHM. Which of the four graphs shows acceleration against time for the same period?
questions.answer: C
steps: Acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph.
The velocity graph starts at zero and rises, so at t = 0 its gradient is a positive maximum: the acceleration starts at its maximum value.
The velocity is at its peak a quarter of a period later, where its gradient is zero, so the acceleration crosses zero there and then goes negative (a = a_max cos omega t).
Only graph C starts at a maximum and falls through zero at a quarter of the period.

questions.question: The graph shows velocity against time for an object in SHM. Which of the four graphs shows displacement against time for the same period?
questions.answer: B
steps: Velocity is the gradient of the displacement-time graph. At t = 0 the velocity is zero, so the displacement is at a maximum or minimum.
Just after t = 0 the velocity is positive, so the displacement is increasing, which means it starts at its negative maximum (x = -A cos omega t).
The velocity is at its peak a quarter of a period later, where the displacement crosses zero going up. Only B starts at a minimum and rises.

questions.question: A mass is forced into oscillation by a vibration generator and the oscillation becomes steady. Which statement is always true? A Amplitude is a maximum. B It oscillates at its natural frequency. C It oscillates at the frequency of the generator. D Energy transfer to the mass is a maximum.
questions.answer: C - the mass oscillates at the frequency of the vibration generator.
steps: In steady forced oscillation the mass oscillates at the driving frequency once transients have died away.
Amplitude and energy transfer are a maximum only at resonance, so A and D are not always true.
The mass does not necessarily oscillate at its natural frequency, so B is not always true.
So the answer is C.

questions.question: State what is meant by simple harmonic motion.
questions.answer: Motion in which the acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and always directed towards equilibrium.
steps: SHM is oscillation in which the acceleration is directly proportional to displacement from a fixed equilibrium position.
The acceleration is always directed towards the equilibrium position.
This gives sinusoidal displacement, velocity and acceleration against time.

questions.question: The building oscillates at 0.17 Hz when the wind blows at a certain speed. Explain why the damper should be designed to oscillate at this frequency.
questions.answer: The damper's natural frequency should match the building frequency, so the damper resonates and takes energy from the building efficiently.
steps: The building oscillates at 0.17 Hz when the wind blows at that speed.
A damper with the same natural frequency is driven at resonance by the building.
At resonance the energy transfer from the building to the damper is a maximum.
So the building's amplitude is reduced effectively.

questions.question: Calculate the stiffness of the spring system for the lead box damper, given its dimensions, the density of lead 11 300 kg m-3 and the oscillation frequency 0.17 Hz.
steps: Volume of the box = 5.20 x 5.20 x 0.90 = 24.3 m^3.
Mass = density x volume = 11 300 x 24.3 = 2.75 x 10^5 kg.
The damper must oscillate at 0.17 Hz, so omega = 2 pi f = 2 pi x 0.17 = 1.07 rad s^-1.
From T = 2 pi sqrt(m / k): k = m omega^2 = 2.75 x 10^5 x (1.07)^2 = 3.1 x 10^5 N m^-1 (the stiffness of the whole spring system).

questions.question: When the building oscillates the floor moves but the lead box tends to remain at rest. Suggest why.
questions.answer: The lead box has a large mass and therefore large inertia, so it resists changes in its motion and tends to stay still.
steps: The lead box has a large mass, so it has large inertia.
A large inertia means a large force is needed to accelerate it.
The springs are soft, so the box moves relative to the floor rather than with it.
This relative motion is what allows the damper to act.

questions.question: As the floor moves, rollers force oil through holes in a steel plate. Explain why this reduces the amplitude of the building's oscillation.
questions.answer: Viscous drag as oil is forced through the holes opposes the motion and dissipates energy as heat, so the amplitude falls.
steps: As the floor moves, the rollers push oil through the holes in the plate.
The oil is viscous, so forcing it through the holes produces a drag force that opposes the motion.
This drag does negative work and converts oscillation energy into thermal energy (damping).
With less energy the building's amplitude of oscillation is reduced.

questions.question: The graph shows force against time for an object in SHM. Which of graphs A to D shows displacement against time over the same interval?
questions.answer: D
steps: The force on the object is F = -kx (equivalently F = ma with a = -omega^2 x), so the displacement graph is the force graph turned upside down.
The force graph starts at zero and rises first, so the displacement starts at zero and goes negative first.
Only D starts at zero and falls. A is the same as the force graph, B starts at a negative value and C starts at a positive maximum.

questions.question: The graph shows force against time for an object in SHM. Which of the four graphs shows velocity against time?
questions.answer: B
steps: The force is proportional to the acceleration (F = ma), and acceleration is the gradient of the velocity-time graph.
The force graph is zero at t = 0, so the velocity gradient is zero there and the velocity is at a maximum or minimum.
Just after t = 0 the force is positive, so the velocity is increasing: the velocity starts at its negative maximum and rises.
The force is at its maximum a quarter of a period later, where the velocity graph is steepest and crossing zero. Only B starts at a minimum and rises.

questions.question: Two pendulums of equal mass, one of length L and one of another length, are given the same initial amplitude. Evaluate the student's suggestion that the maximum kinetic energy of one is four times that of the other.
questions.answer: The suggestion is not correct: the maximum kinetic energy of the L/2 pendulum is only about twice (not four times) that of the L pendulum.
steps: The diagram shows both bobs pulled aside by the same horizontal distance A (same amplitude), and the masses are equal. For small swings E_k max = 1/2 m omega^2 A^2, with omega^2 = g / length.
For the pendulum of length L, omega^2 = g / L. For the pendulum of length L/2, omega^2 = 2g / L, which is twice as large.
m and A are the same, so E_k max is proportional to omega^2 and is doubled, not quadrupled.
Check with energy: for a small swing the bob rises by h = A^2 / (2 x length), so halving the length doubles h and doubles the maximum kinetic energy m g h.
A factor of four would be right only if omega were doubled. Halving the length multiplies omega by only sqrt(2), so v_max rises by sqrt(2) and E_k by (sqrt 2)^2 = 2.

questions.question: The graph shows acceleration against displacement from equilibrium for an object. Explain how the graph shows that the object moves with simple harmonic motion.
questions.answer: The graph is a straight line through the origin with a negative gradient, so a is proportional to -x: the acceleration is proportional to the displacement and always directed towards equilibrium, which is the definition of SHM.
steps: A straight line through the origin means a is directly proportional to x.
The negative gradient means the acceleration is always in the opposite direction to the displacement, that is towards the equilibrium position (a = -omega^2 x), which is the condition for SHM.

questions.question: For the object of mass 0.25 kg whose acceleration-displacement graph is shown, calculate its maximum kinetic energy.
steps: The gradient of the a-x graph is -omega^2: omega^2 = 0.70 / 0.040 = 17.5 s^-2, so omega = 4.18 rad s^-1.
The graph extends to x = +/-0.040 m, so the amplitude is A = 0.040 m.

questions.question: Sketch a graph on the axes provided to show how the kinetic energy of the object varies with displacement x. No further calculations are needed.
questions.answer: An inverted parabola (hill shape) symmetric about the vertical axis, with maximum kinetic energy of 3.5 mJ at x = 0 and falling to zero at x = +0.040 m and x = -0.040 m.
steps: E_k = 1/2 m omega^2 (A^2 - x^2), which is a quadratic in x with a negative x^2 term, so the graph is an inverted parabola.
At x = 0 the kinetic energy is at its maximum (3.5 mJ from part (i)); at x = +/-A = +/-0.040 m it is zero.
The curve is symmetrical about the E_k axis, never goes negative, and meets the x axis at +/-0.040 m.

questions.question: Explain the cause of the large swaying motion of the Millennium Bridge when people walked across it, and the effect of the dampers fitted to it.
questions.answer: Pedestrians walking in step forced the bridge at its natural frequency (resonance); dampers dissipate energy and reduce the amplitude.
steps: Pedestrians walking across the bridge exerted periodic sideways forces on it.
Their walking frequency matched the natural frequency of the bridge, so resonance occurred.
Energy was transferred efficiently into the bridge, giving a large swaying amplitude.
The dampers exert a force opposing the motion of the bridge and dissipate energy as heat.
Damping therefore reduces the amplitude of the swaying and the resonance effect.

questions.question: Ductile materials are used in buildings to reduce the amplitude of forced oscillations during an earthquake. Which is the reason? A stiff, B strong, C deform elastically, D deform plastically.
questions.answer: D - they deform plastically, dissipating energy.
steps: Ductile materials can undergo large permanent (plastic) deformation.
Plastic deformation dissipates the oscillation energy as heat, which damps the motion.
Elastic deformation stores and returns energy, so C is wrong.
Stiffness and strength do not remove energy, so the answer is D.

questions.question: Plasticine is added to a paper-cone pendulum to increase its mass and it is set into oscillation again. Which is correct? A The frequency has decreased. B The period has increased. C The amplitude decreased more quickly. D The amplitude decreased more slowly.
questions.answer: D - the amplitude decreases more slowly.
steps: The period of a simple pendulum depends on length and g, not on mass, so frequency and period do not change (A and B are wrong).
The same air resistance acts on the heavier bob, which has more inertia, so its velocity changes more slowly.
Energy is therefore lost more slowly relative to the oscillation, and the amplitude decreases more slowly.
So the answer is D.

questions.question: A 0.35 kg mass on a spring has period 0.95 s. After an extra mass is added the period is 1.15 s. Calculate the added mass.
questions.answer: Added mass = 0.16 kg.
steps: Period T = 2 pi sqrt(m/k), so T^2 is proportional to m with k constant.
The added mass is about 0.16 kg.

questions.question: A woman of mass 67 kg oscillates on an elastic rope with period 1.50 s. A second person of mass 72 kg is then attached and the same rope is used. Calculate the new period.
questions.answer: Period = 2.16 s.
steps: The rope's stiffness is constant: k = 4 pi^2 m / T^2 = 4 pi^2 x 67 / 1.50^2 = 1.18 x 10^3 N m-1.
The new total mass is m = 67 + 72 = 139 kg.
T = 2 pi sqrt(m / k) = 2 pi sqrt(139 / 1176) = 2.16 s.
So the period of the two people is 2.16 s.

questions.question: A mass is driven into oscillation and resonance takes place. Which statement is not correct? A The amplitude is a maximum. B The frequency of oscillation is a maximum. C The mass is driven at its natural frequency. D The transfer of energy to the mass is a maximum.
questions.answer: B - the frequency of oscillation is the driving frequency, not a maximum.
steps: At resonance the amplitude and the energy transfer are both a maximum, so A and D are correct.
The mass is driven at its natural frequency at resonance, so C is correct.
The frequency of oscillation equals the driving frequency; it is not a maximum, so B is not correct.
So the answer is B.

questions.question: The graph shows displacement against time for an object in SHM. Which of the four graphs shows velocity against time for the same period?
questions.answer: D
steps: Velocity is the gradient of the displacement-time graph. The displacement graph starts at its negative maximum, where the gradient is zero, so the velocity starts at zero.
Just after t = 0 the displacement is increasing, so the velocity is positive: the velocity graph starts at zero and rises (v = A omega sin omega t).
Only graph D starts at zero and rises. A starts at a positive maximum, B starts at a negative value and C starts at zero but falls.

questions.question: The graph shows displacement against time for an object in SHM. Which of the four graphs shows acceleration against time?
questions.answer: A
steps: In SHM a = -omega^2 x, so the acceleration graph is the displacement graph turned upside down (same period).
The displacement graph starts at its negative maximum, so the acceleration starts at its positive maximum and falls.
Only graph A starts at a positive maximum and falls. B starts at a negative value, C starts at zero going down and D starts at zero going up.

questions.question: State the conditions for an object to oscillate with simple harmonic motion, applied to the car body on its suspension.
questions.answer: Acceleration is proportional to displacement from equilibrium and is always directed towards equilibrium.
steps: The acceleration must be directly proportional to the displacement from equilibrium.
The acceleration must always be directed towards the equilibrium position.
The restoring force of the suspension provides this acceleration.
Together these conditions give simple harmonic motion.

questions.question: The graph shows how the vertical displacement of the car body varies with time. Determine the maximum velocity of the car body.
questions.answer: v_max = 0.47 m s^-1
steps: From the graph the amplitude is A = 3.0 cm = 0.030 m.
The peaks are at 0.2 s, 0.6 s and 1.0 s, so the period is T = 0.40 s and omega = 2 pi / T = 2 pi / 0.40 = 15.7 rad s^-1.

questions.question: Explain how damping causes the amplitude of oscillation of the car body to decrease.
questions.answer: Damping forces do negative work, dissipating the oscillation energy as heat, so the amplitude decreases.
steps: Damping forces oppose the motion of the car body and do negative work on it.
The energy of the oscillation is converted into thermal energy.
With less energy the amplitude decreases on each cycle.
